activities.title: PRIMM — summing a list
activities.description: Predict, Run, Investigate and Make, all about one short accumulator function. Predict and Make are marked by hand; Investigate is marked automatically.

config.title: Predict
config.prompt:
Read the program above. Do NOT run it yet.

What will it print? Write down the number, and one sentence saying how you worked it out.
config.instructions: There are no marks for being right — there are marks for saying what you actually think.

config.title: Run
config.prompt:
Run the program. It prints:

8

Compare that with what you predicted. Were you right? If you were not, what did you miss?
config.instructions: This step carries no marks. It exists so you look at the gap before moving on.

config.title: Investigate
config.instructions: Now pull the program apart. Every question is about the code above.

questions.stem: How many times does the body of the for loop run?

options.text: Three times — once for each item in the list
Eight times — once for each unit of the total

questions.stem: What would the program print if the line `runningTotal = 0` were moved inside the loop, indented to the same level as the line below it?
What is the purpose of the variable `runningTotal`?

options.text: It counts how many numbers are in the list
It holds the sum so far, and survives from one pass of the loop to the next
It stores the current item being looked at
It is only there to be returned at the end

questions.stem: Why is `return runningTotal` outside the loop rather than inside it?

options.text: Python does not allow return inside a for loop
Inside the loop it would return after the first number, before the rest were added
It makes no difference where it goes
Indentation is only a style choice here

i1.explanation: `for n in numbers` runs the body once per item, and the list [3, 1, 4] has three items.

i2.explanation: Resetting the accumulator inside the loop throws away the running total on every pass, so only the last number survives — 4. This is the single most common accumulator bug.

i3.explanation: It is the accumulator. It has to be created before the loop precisely so that it persists across passes.

i4.explanation: A return exits the function immediately. Inside the loop it would fire on the first pass and return 3.

config.title: Make
config.prompt:
Write your own function called `largest(numbers)` that returns the biggest number in a list, using the same accumulator pattern as `total`.

Then answer this in a sentence: starting your accumulator at 0 works for a total. Why is 0 a bad starting value for `largest`, and what would you use instead?
config.instructions: Your teacher reads and marks this one. Write the code out in full.
